For very short‑latency (dense) needs, allow such cuts only when the left fragment, taken alone, is a coherent, non‑contradictory piece and the right fragment begins with material that can be translated independently (for example a noun head, clause marker, or clause‑initial predicate). Prefer cuts that align with morphological or phrase boundaries and avoid splitting inside a lexical word; in other words, describe and prefer GOOD dense cuts (interpretable left piece, attachable right piece) instead of a blanket ban.
